scope: Schema-valid successor for the invalid historical wache-koenig packet. Directly re-read exact archived Drive source bytes for wache-koenig.py and freigabe, verified SHA-256 against the canonical archive manifest, and preserved source-only/historical scope. No runtime reachability or whole-system enforcement credit.

atoms.what_it_does: Parses a PreToolUse-style JSON event, returns allow for every non-Bash tool, classifies Bash command text, exits 2 for hard-deny classes or ticket-required commands without a valid ticket, and exits 0 otherwise. When wired as a blocking PreToolUse hook this is genuine pre-execution blocking for its Bash scope.
open_questions: Recover exact scheduler/settings registration and ordering.
Identify typed enforcement coverage for non-Bash state-changing tools.

atoms.what_it_does: Defines hard-deny and ticket-required regex classes anchored to command positions, strips heredoc/string data before primary checks, separately reinspects ssh/scp/rsync and shell -c inner commands, and adds database destructive-operation detection.
open_questions: Port useful cases as typed intent/resource/capability regression fixtures rather than retaining regex as canonical authority.

atoms.what_it_does: Hashes exact command text, loads the matching ticket, checks full hash and validity window, deletes expired tickets, and unlinks a valid ticket before returning allow, making the grant one-shot in the ordinary path.
open_questions: Successor should bind typed EffectRequest, resource identity, generation, owner grant identity, policy version and exact executor lease atomically.

atoms.what_it_does: Requires /dev/tty, two sequential fresh typed challenges with timing checks, applies an optional deletion-size bound, then writes a mode-0600 command-hash ticket with 10-minute delayed activation and 20-minute validity.
open_questions: Replace behavioral typing heuristics with explicit authenticated owner/capability grant while preserving out-of-model separation, scope binding, expiry and one-shot consumption.

hypotheses: Frankenstein 2.0 should preserve the architectural split: model/candidate requests never self-authorize; a deterministic executor boundary consumes a separately minted, scope-bound owner/capability decision before execution.

The historical command-hash ticket is a useful donor for one-shot capability lease semantics, but the successor must bind typed EffectRequest + immutable invocation identity + request digest + resource identity + generation + policy/executor identity.
counterhypotheses: A newer host-level permission layer may already supersede wache-koenig and cover more tool classes; exact source plus live wiring would outrank this historical donor.

For shell-only commands, raw-command tickets may remain simpler than a larger typed object; acceptance must test aliasing, cwd/environment/resource resolution, concurrent identical attempts and cross-tool effects before retaining that design.
contradictions: Current donor stern.py ordinary admission is nonblocking bookkeeping, while historical wache-koenig source contains genuine Bash-scoped pre-execution blocking when registered; these are different authority classes.
Historical wache-koenig has zero non-Bash coverage by design, so it cannot establish one complete effect authority for Write/Edit/NotebookEdit or other effectful tools.
Source and archive identity are exact, but scheduler registration/order and runtime reachability remain unproven.
critical_unknowns: Exact settings/scheduler entry and ordering that registered this wache-koenig snapshot.
Whether current Frankenstein 0.7 retains this exact watcher, a successor, host permissions, or no equivalent gate.
Whether all state-changing tool classes converge on one deterministic execution boundary.
Atomicity of ticket consumption under concurrent identical attempts.

recommended_next_spans.reason: Prove actual hook registration/order and matcher scope for wache-koenig.
Trace realtime function-call/tool executor permission boundary and compare it against hook-based Bash gating.
Determine whether a newer deterministic gate supersedes the historical watcher and covers non-Bash effects.
